original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
bhūya eva mahābāho śrṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ|
yatte'haṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord (śrī bhagavān) said: Hear once more, mighty-armed one, my supreme word (paramaṃ vacaḥ), which I shall speak to you, who take delight, out of a wish for your welfare (hita).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prīyamāṇāya: 'to you who are pleased/delighted' — the verse does not say by what; commentators take it as delight in hearing the Lord's words. 'Once more' (bhūya eva) ties the chapter to the teaching of the preceding chapters.

original.text:
na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ|
ahamādirhi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Neither the hosts of the gods (sura) nor the great seers (maharṣi) know my origin (prabhava); for I am in every way the beginning (ādi) of the gods and of the great seers.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prabhava: 'coming forth, origin'. Śaṅkara also allows reading it as prabhāva, 'surpassing power, majesty'. The reason given (hi) is that the Lord precedes those who would have to know his origin.

original.text:
yo māmajamanādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram|
asammūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whoever knows me as unborn (aja) and without beginning (anādi), the great lord of the world (loka-maheśvara), he among mortals is undeluded (asaṃmūḍha) and is set free from all sins (pāpa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
buddhirjñānamasaṃmohaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ|
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavo'bhāvo bhayaṃ cābhayameva ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Understanding (buddhi), knowledge (jñāna), freedom from delusion (asaṃmoha), forbearance (kṣamā), truthfulness (satya), restraint (dama), calm (śama), pleasure (sukha) and pain (duḥkha), coming-to-be and ceasing-to-be (bhava, abhāva), fear (bhaya) and fearlessness (abhaya) — (the sentence continues in 10.5: these states of beings arise from me alone).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 10.4–5 form one sentence whose predicate is in 10.5. bhava/abhāva may be 'arising and passing away' or 'being and non-being'. Opposites (pleasure and pain, fear and fearlessness, fame and ill-fame) are all included among the states that come from the Lord.

original.text:
ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭistapo dānaṃ yaśo'yaśaḥ|
bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Non-harming (ahiṃsā), evenness (samatā), contentment (tuṣṭi), austerity (tapas), giving (dāna), fame and ill-fame (yaśas, ayaśas) — the states (bhāva) of beings, in all their different kinds, arise from me alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Completes the list begun in 10.4; 'from me alone' (matta eva) governs the whole list.

original.text:
maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavastathā|
madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The seven great seers (maharṣi) of old and likewise the Manus — the verse also speaks of 'four' (see notes) — having my nature (madbhāva), were born from (my) mind (mānasa); from them are these creatures (prajā) in the world.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The words maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavas tathā are grouped differently: 'the seven great seers of old and the four Manus' (Śaṅkara's reading), or 'the seven great seers, the four ancient ones (taken by some commentators as Sanaka and his brothers) and the Manus'. madbhāvāḥ: 'sharing my being/power', or 'whose disposition is directed to me'. mānasāḥ: mind-born; the verse does not say whose mind, though the context makes it the Lord's.

original.text:
etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ|
so'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whoever knows in truth (tattvataḥ) this manifestation (vibhūti) and yoga of mine is joined with unwavering yoga (avikampa yoga); of this there is no doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'My yoga' (yogaṃ mama) is the Lord's own yoga — cf. 'my sovereign yoga' (yogam aiśvaram) at 9.5 and 11.8; commentators gloss it as his lordly power or the joining by which he manifests. The verse does not define the knower's 'unwavering yoga'.

original.text:
ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate|
iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the origin (prabhava) of all; from me everything proceeds (pravartate). Understanding this, the wise (budha), endowed with bhāva, worship (bhajante) me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: bhāva-samanvitāḥ: 'filled with loving feeling' or 'filled with conviction / intent on the highest truth'; commentators differ. The worship follows from the understanding (iti matvā).

original.text:
maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam|
kathayantaśca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: With their thought (citta) on me, their life-breaths (prāṇa) gone into me, awakening one another (bodhayantaḥ parasparam) and always speaking of me, they are content and they delight.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The subject continues from 10.8 (the wise who worship). madgataprāṇāḥ: 'whose prāṇas (life-breaths, or the senses called prāṇas) have gone into me', or 'whose very life is given to me'; commentators differ. tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca: they are satisfied and take delight.

original.text:
teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam|
dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena māmupayānti te
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: To them, ever yoked (satata-yukta), worshipping with love (prīti-pūrvakam), I give that yoga of understanding (buddhi-yoga) by which they come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
teṣāmevānukampārthamahamajñānajaṃ tamaḥ|
nāśayāmyātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Out of compassion (anukampā) for them alone, I, abiding in (their) own being (ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ; or: remaining in my own state), destroy the darkness (tamas) born of ignorance (ajñāna) with the shining lamp of knowledge (jñāna-dīpa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmabhāvasthaḥ: the reflexive may refer to the devotees ('abiding in their inner being' — the reading commentators commonly give) or to the speaker ('remaining in my own state'). tamas here is 'darkness', the image paired with the lamp; the verse does not name the guṇa.

original.text:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān|
puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyamādidevamajaṃ vibhum
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: You are the supreme brahman (paraṃ brahma), the supreme abode (paraṃ dhāma), the supreme purifier (pavitraṃ paramam); the eternal, divine Person (puruṣa), the first god (ādideva), unborn (aja), all-pervading (vibhu) —
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 10.12–13 form one sentence. dhāman: abode, station, or light. pavitraṃ paramam: 'the supreme purifier' or 'supreme purity'.

original.text:
āhustvāmṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣirnāradastathā|
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — so all the seers (ṛṣi) declare you, and the divine seer Nārada, Asita Devala and Vyāsa; and you yourself tell me so.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: asito devalaḥ is usually taken as one sage, Asita Devala; it can also be read as two names (Asita and Devala). Arjuna grounds his acknowledgement both on the testimony of the seers and on Kṛṣṇa's own word.

original.text:
sarvametadṛtaṃ manye yanmāṃ vadasi keśava|
na hi te bhagavan vyakitaṃ vidurdevā na dānavāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: All this that you tell me, Keśava, I hold to be true (ṛta); for neither the gods nor the dānavas know your manifestation (vyakti), Blessed One (bhagavan).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The edition's text reads 'vyakitaṃ' (an encoding slip for vyaktiṃ, Devanāgarī व्यक्तिं). vyakti: manifestation, appearance, distinct form. The verse echoes 10.2 (not even the gods know him).

original.text:
svayamevātmanā'tmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama|
bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You yourself know yourself by yourself (svayam evātmanātmānaṃ vettha), highest Person (puruṣottama), source of beings (bhūta-bhāvana), lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmanā ātmānam is reflexive: the Lord knows himself by himself, whereas gods and seers do not know him (10.2, 10.14).

original.text:
vaktumarhasyaśeṣeṇa divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ|
yābhirvibhūtibhirlokānimāṃstvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You should tell without remainder your own divine manifestations (ātma-vibhūti), the manifestations by which you stand pervading these worlds.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: divyā hy ātmavibhūtayaḥ: 'for (your) own manifestations are divine' — the same phrase returns in the Lord's reply (10.19). ātma- is reflexive: the Lord's own manifestations.

original.text:
kathaṃ vidyāmahaṃ yogiṃstvāṃ sadā paricintayan|
keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo'si bhagavanmayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: How may I know you, O yogin, while constantly contemplating you (paricintayan)? And in which various beings or states (bhāva) are you to be contemplated (cintya) by me, Blessed One?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Arjuna addresses Kṛṣṇa as 'yogin'. The question sets the purpose of the list that follows (10.20–39): the manifestations are named as places where the Lord is to be thought of.

original.text:
vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana|
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi śrṛṇvato nāsti me'mṛtam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Tell me again, in detail, your own yoga (ātmano yogam) and manifestation (vibhūti), Janārdana; for hearing (your) nectar (amṛta) I have no satiety.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmanaḥ is reflexive (your own yoga). 'Again' (bhūyaḥ) refers to what was told briefly (e.g. 10.7–8, or earlier at 7.8–12 and 9.16–19).

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ|
prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Well then, I shall tell you my divine manifestations (vibhūti) — the principal ones (prādhānyataḥ), best of the Kurus; for there is no end to my extent (vistara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ|
ahamādiśca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am the self (ātman), Guḍākeśa, seated in the resting-place (āśaya) of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Here ātmā is a predicate noun ('I am the self'), not a reflexive. āśaya: seat, receptacle, resting-place — commentators take it as the heart or inner region of beings. The first named 'manifestation' is thus the self within all, before the list of the best in each class.

original.text:
ādityānāmahaṃ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṃ raviraṃśumān|
marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of lights (jyotis), the radiant sun (ravi); of the Maruts I am Marīci; of the lunar mansions (nakṣatra), I am the moon (śaśin).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The pattern 'of X I am Y' names the chief of each class as the Lord's manifestation (cf. 10.19 'the principal ones'). The Marīci named here is one of the Maruts; the verse does not identify him with the mind-born sage of that name.

original.text:
vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ|
indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; of the gods, Vāsava (Indra); of the faculties (indriya) I am the mind (manas); of beings I am sentience (cetanā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: manas is counted here among the indriyas (as its chief). cetanā: the awareness or sentience found in living beings; commentators gloss it in different ways. The verse keeps manas and cetanā distinct.

original.text:
rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām|
vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the Rudras I am Śaṅkara; of the yakṣas and rākṣasas, the lord of wealth (vitteśa); of the Vasus I am fire (pāvaka, 'the purifier'); of peaks, Meru.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Śaṅkara here is a name of the chief Rudra (Śiva), not the later teacher. The lord of wealth is traditionally Kubera, who is not named in the verse.

original.text:
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim|
senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know me, Pārtha, as the chief of household priests (purodhas), Bṛhaspati; of generals I am Skanda; of bodies of water, the ocean (sāgara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgurahaṃ girāmasmyekamakṣaram|
yajñānāṃ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the great seers I am Bhṛgu; of utterances (gir), I am the one syllable (ekam akṣaram); of sacrifices, I am the sacrifice of muttered recitation (japa-yajña); of immovable things, the Himālaya.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse does not spell out 'the one syllable'; the Gītā itself names 'the one syllable, brahman' as oṃ at 8.13. akṣara here means 'syllable', not 'the imperishable' of 8.3, 11.37 and 12.3. Japa is counted as a kind of sacrifice (yajña).

original.text:
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ|
gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of all trees, the aśvattha; of the divine seers (devarṣi), Nārada; of the gandharvas, Citraratha; of the perfected ones (siddha), the sage (muni) Kapila.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse calls Kapila a muni among the siddhas; it does not mention Sāṃkhya here. The aśvattha is simply the chief of trees in this verse (contrast its use as the image of saṃsāra at 15.1–3).

original.text:
uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam|
airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know me as Uccaiḥśravas among horses, born of the nectar (amṛtodbhava); as Airāvata among lordly elephants; and among men, as the king (narādhipa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: amṛtodbhava: 'arisen from the nectar' — commentators refer it to the churning of the ocean for the nectar, which the verse does not narrate.

original.text:
āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk|
prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt (vajra); of cows, the wish-yielding one (kāmadhuk); I am Kandarpa, the begetter (prajana); of serpents (sarpa), I am Vāsuki.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prajanaḥ: 'the one who begets' — commentators take Kandarpa (Kāma) here as desire in its procreative function; the verse says only 'Kandarpa the begetter'.

original.text:
anantaścāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasāmaham|
pitṛ़ṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatāmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the nāgas I am Ananta; of the water-dwellers (yādas), Varuṇa; of the ancestors (pitṛ), Aryaman; of those who restrain (saṃyamatām), I am Yama.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse names nāgas separately from the sarpas of 10.28 without explaining the difference (commentators supply one). saṃyamatām: 'of those who control / restrain' (or 'punish'). The edition's text shows an encoding artefact in 'pitṛ़ṇām' (for pitṝṇām).

original.text:
prahlādaścāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham|
mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro'haṃ vainateyaśca pakṣiṇām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the daityas I am Prahlāda; of those that reckon (kalayatām), I am time (kāla); of beasts, the lord of beasts (mṛgendra); of birds, Vainateya (Garuḍa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: kalayatām: 'of those who count/calculate', or 'of those who impel/subdue'; commentators differ. Time appears three times in the chapter and the next (10.30, 10.33, 11.32).

original.text:
pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham|
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of purifiers (pavatām) I am the wind (pavana); of the bearers of weapons, Rāma; of the water-creatures (jhaṣa), the makara; of rivers (srotas), I am Jāhnavī (the Gaṅgā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: pavatām may be 'of purifiers' or 'of those that move swiftly'. The verse names only 'Rāma'; commentators commonly identify him with Rāma, son of Daśaratha.

original.text:
sargāṇāmādirantaśca madhyaṃ caivāhamarjuna|
adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatāmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of creations (sarga) I am the beginning and the end and also the middle, Arjuna; of the sciences (vidyā), the knowledge concerning the self (adhyātma-vidyā); of those who speak in debate (pravadatām), I am the discussion (vāda).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sarga: emanations / created things. adhyātma-vidyā: knowledge pertaining to the self (ātman). vāda is explained by commentators as the discussion aimed at settling the truth, as distinct from wrangling (jalpa) and cavil (vitaṇḍā) — a classification the verse itself does not state. pravadatām may also be 'of speakers'.

original.text:
akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca|
ahamevākṣayaḥ kālo dhātā'haṃ viśvatomukhaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of letters (akṣara) I am the letter a (akāra); of the compounds (sāmāsika), the copulative (dvandva); I alone am imperishable time (akṣaya kāla); I am the ordainer (dhātṛ) facing in every direction (viśvatomukha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: akṣara here means 'letter / syllable'. dhātṛ: placer, sustainer, or dispenser (commentators: the dispenser of the fruits of action). 'I alone am imperishable time' differs from the 'time of those that reckon' in 10.30; commentators relate it to the Lord as time itself or as the time that devours time.

original.text:
mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām|
kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I am death (mṛtyu) that seizes all, and the arising (udbhava) of those that are yet to be; of the feminine (nārīṇām), I am fame (kīrti), fortune (śrī), speech (vāc), memory (smṛti), retentive intelligence (medhā), steadfastness (dhṛti) and forbearance (kṣamā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: nārīṇām: literally 'of women / of feminine ones'; the seven names are feminine nouns, and commentators read them either as excellences found in women or as the goddesses who bear these names. smṛti here is 'memory', not the class of remembered scripture.

original.text:
bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasāmaham|
māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'hamṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the sāman chants I am the Bṛhat-sāman; of metres (chandas), the gāyatrī; of months, Mārgaśīrṣa; of seasons, the bringer of flowers (kusumākara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: kusumākara, 'the mine of flowers', is taken as spring (vasanta), which the verse does not name.

original.text:
dyūtaṃ chalayatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham|
jayo'smi vyavasāyo'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatāmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of those who deceive (chalayatām) I am gambling (dyūta); I am the splendour (tejas) of the splendid; I am victory, I am resolve (vyavasāya); I am the sattva of those who possess it (sattvavat).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sattva here may be 'goodness' (commentators: the sāttvika quality) or 'strength, courage'; the verse does not name the three guṇas. The verse counts even the deceivers' chief means among the manifestations without commenting on its worth.

original.text:
vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ|
munīnāmapyahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; of the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya (Arjuna); of the sages (muni) too I am Vyāsa; of the seer-poets (kavi), the seer Uśanas.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The speaker names himself (Vāsudeva, the Vṛṣṇi) and his hearer (Dhanañjaya) among his own manifestations; Vyāsa is the sage already cited as a witness in 10.13.

original.text:
daṇḍo damayatāmasmi nītirasmi jigīṣatām|
maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatāmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Of those who subdue (damayatām) I am the rod of punishment (daṇḍa); of those who seek victory, right policy (nīti); of secret things (guhya), I am silence (mauna); I am the knowledge (jñāna) of the knowers.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yaccāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tadahamarjuna|
na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And whatever is the seed (bīja) of all beings, that am I, Arjuna; there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
nānto'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ paraṃtapa|
eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūtervistaro mayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: There is no end to my divine manifestations (vibhūti), scorcher of foes; this account of the extent of my manifestation has been given by me only by way of indication (uddeśataḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā|
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejoṃ'śasaṃbhavam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever being (sattva) is endowed with manifest power (vibhūtimat), glorious (śrīmat) or mighty (ūrjita) — know that it has arisen from a portion (aṃśa) of my splendour (tejas).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sattva here means 'a being, an existent thing', not the guṇa. The verse turns the list into a rule that can be applied to anything excellent.

original.text:
athavā bahunaitena kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna|
viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśena sthito jagat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But what is the use to you, Arjuna, of knowing all this at such length? I stand supporting (viṣṭabhya) this entire world with a single portion (ekāṃśa) (of myself).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse does not say what lies beyond the portion that supports the world; compare the Puruṣa hymn, where all beings are a quarter of the Person (ṚV 10.90.3).

paraphrase: Chapter 10 is the Lord's account of his manifestations (vibhūti), given, as he says, out of a wish for Arjuna's welfare (10.1). Movements: (1) 10.1–11 — the Lord announces his supreme word; neither gods nor great seers know his origin, since he is their beginning (10.2); whoever knows him as unborn, beginningless lord of the world is undeluded and freed from sins (10.3); all the states of beings, and the seven great seers and the Manus, come from him (10.4–6); knowing his vibhūti and yoga brings unwavering yoga (10.7); knowing him as the origin of all, the wise worship him with their thought on him, speaking of him to one another (10.8–9), and to these he gives the yoga of understanding and destroys the darkness born of ignorance (10.10–11). (2) 10.12–18 — Arjuna acknowledges him as the supreme brahman and eternal Person, as the seers (Nārada, Asita Devala, Vyāsa) proclaim (10.12–13); only he knows himself by himself (10.15); Arjuna asks to be told his manifestations and in which things he is to be contemplated (10.16–18). (3) 10.19–39 — the Lord names his principal manifestations: first the self seated in all beings and the beginning, middle and end of beings (10.20), then the chief of each class of gods, seers, beings, things, sounds, times and qualities (10.21–38), and finally the seed of all beings without which nothing exists (10.39). (4) 10.40–42 — there is no end to his manifestations; whatever is glorious or mighty springs from a portion of his splendour; he stands supporting the whole world with a single portion. Purpose as the chapter states it: that Arjuna may know the Lord and contemplate him in all excellent things (10.17, 10.41).
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam|
yattvayoktaṃ vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: By the word you have spoken out of favour to me (mad-anugraha) — the supreme secret (guhya) called adhyātma, concerning the self — this delusion (moha) of mine is gone.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse does not say which part of the preceding teaching is meant by 'the secret called adhyātma'. anugraha: favour, kindness shown to Arjuna.

original.text:
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā|
tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For I have heard from you in detail of the arising and the passing away (bhava, apyaya) of beings, lotus-eyed one, and also of your imperishable greatness (māhātmya).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvara|
draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It is just as you have described yourself (ātmānam), supreme lord (parameśvara); (yet) I wish to see your sovereign form (rūpam aiśvaram), highest Person (puruṣottama).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmānam is reflexive ('as you have spoken of yourself'), not the doctrinal self. Arjuna accepts the spoken account and asks to see what was described.

original.text:
manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho|
yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayā'tmānamavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: If you think that it can be seen by me, lord (prabhu), then, lord of yoga (yogeśvara), show me yourself (ātmānam), the imperishable (avyaya).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmānam is reflexive: 'show yourself', qualified as imperishable (avyaya). The request is conditional on the Lord's judgment of Arjuna's capacity.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ|
nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Behold, Pārtha, my forms (rūpa), by hundreds and by thousands — manifold, divine, of many colours and shapes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśivanau marutastathā|
bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyā'ścaryāṇi bhārata
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Behold the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins and the Maruts; behold many wonders never seen before, Bhārata.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ihaikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram|
mama dehe guḍākeśa yaccānyaddraṣṭumicchasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Behold here today, Guḍākeśa, the entire world, moving and unmoving, standing as one (ekastha) in my body (deha), and whatever else you wish to see.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā|
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But you cannot see me with just this eye of your own; I give you a divine eye (divyaṃ cakṣuḥ) — behold my sovereign yoga (yogam aiśvaram).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The ordinary eye (svacakṣus) is declared insufficient; the capacity to see is given by the Lord.

original.text:
evamuktvā tato rājanmahāyogeśvaro hariḥ|
darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpamaiśvaram
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus, O king, Hari, the great lord of yoga (mahā-yogeśvara), then showed Pārtha his supreme, sovereign form (paramaṃ rūpam aiśvaram).
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam|
anekadivyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: (A form) with many mouths and eyes, many wondrous aspects, many divine ornaments, many divine weapons raised,
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 11.10–11 describe the form in one run of attributes (grammatically objects of 'showed' in 11.9).

original.text:
divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam|
sarvāścaryamayaṃ devamanantaṃ viśvatomukham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, full of every wonder — the god (deva), endless (ananta), facing in every direction (viśvatomukha).
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā|
yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: If the light of a thousand suns were to rise all at once in the sky, that might be like the light of that great being (mahātman).
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The comparison is hypothetical ('if ... it might be like'): the light is described as exceeding ordinary measure.

original.text:
tatraikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktamanekadhā|
apaśyaddevadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavastadā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: There, in the body of the god of gods, the Pāṇḍava then saw the entire world, divided in many ways, standing as one (ekastha).
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā dhanañjayaḥ|
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Then Dhanañjaya, filled with amazement (vismaya), his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the god and, with joined palms, spoke.
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
paśyāmi devāṃstava deva dehe
sarvāṃstathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṅghān|
brahmāṇamīśaṃ kamalāsanastha
mṛṣīṃśca sarvānuragāṃśca divyān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: I see in your body, O god, all the gods and the hosts of the various kinds of beings; Brahmā, the lord (īśa), seated on the lotus-seat, all the seers (ṛṣi) and the divine serpents (uraga).
speaker: Arjuna

original.text:
anekabāhūdaravaktranetraṃ
paśyāmi tvāṃ sarvato'nantarūpam|
nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punastavādiṃ
paśyāmi viśveśvara viśvarūpa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: With many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes, I see you, of endless form on every side; no end, no middle, nor yet any beginning of you do I see, lord of all (viśveśvara), whose form is all (viśvarūpa).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca
tejorāśiṃ sarvatodīptimantam|
paśyāmi tvāṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ samantā
ddīptānalārkadyutimaprameyam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I see you wearing a crown, bearing a mace and a discus, a mass of splendour (tejo-rāśi) shining on every side, hard to look upon, all around with the radiance of blazing fire and sun, immeasurable (aprameya).
speaker: Arjuna

original.text:
tvamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ
tvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam|
tvamavyayaḥ śāśvatadharmagoptā
sanātanastvaṃ puruṣo mato me
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You are the imperishable (akṣara), the supreme that is to be known (veditavya); you are the supreme resting-place (nidhāna) of this universe; you are the unchanging (avyaya) guardian of the eternal dharma (śāśvata-dharma); you are, I hold, the everlasting Person (sanātana puruṣa).
speaker: Arjuna

original.text:
anādimadhyāntamanantavīrya
manantabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetram|
paśyāmi tvāṃ dīptahutāśavaktram
svatejasā viśvamidaṃ tapantam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Without beginning, middle or end, of endless power, of endless arms, with moon and sun for eyes, I see you, your mouth a blazing fire, heating this universe with your own splendour (tejas).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṃ hi
vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaśca sarvāḥ|
dṛṣṭvā'dbhutaṃ rūpamugraṃ tavedaṃ
lokatrayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahātman
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For this space between heaven and earth, and all the directions, are pervaded by you alone; seeing this wondrous, fierce (ugra) form of yours, the three worlds tremble, great being (mahātman).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
amī hi tvāṃ surasaṅghāḥ viśanti
kecidbhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti|
svastītyuktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ
stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Those hosts of gods enter into you; some, afraid, praise you with joined palms; saying 'may it be well' (svasti), hosts of great seers and perfected ones (siddha) praise you with abundant hymns.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā
viśve'śivanau marutaścoṣmapāśca|
gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghā
vīkṣante tvāṃ vismitāścaiva sarve
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus and the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts and the Ūṣmapas, the hosts of gandharvas, yakṣas, asuras and siddhas — all gaze upon you, amazed.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ūṣmapāḥ, 'drinkers of the warm (portion)', are taken by commentators as a class of ancestors (pitṛ).

original.text:
rūpaṃ mahatte bahuvaktranetraṃ
mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam|
bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ
dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitāstathā'ham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, mighty-armed one, with many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies, terrible with many tusks, the worlds are shaken (pravyathita), and so am I.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptamanekavarṇaṃ
vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetram|
dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā
dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing, many-coloured, with gaping mouths and wide blazing eyes, I am shaken in my inner self (pravyathitāntarātmā) and find neither steadiness (dhṛti) nor calm (śama), Viṣṇu.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: antarātman here is Arjuna's own inner being (reflexive: 'my inner self'), not the doctrinal self. Arjuna addresses Kṛṣṇa as Viṣṇu (also 11.30).

original.text:
daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni
dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni|
diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Having seen your mouths, terrible with tusks, like the fire of time (kālānala), I do not know the directions and find no shelter (śarma). Be gracious (prasīda), lord of gods, abode of the world (jagannivāsa).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: kālānala: 'the fire of time', taken by commentators as the fire that consumes the worlds at their dissolution. 'I do not know the directions': Arjuna has lost his bearings.

original.text:
amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ
sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ|
bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathā'sau
sahāsmadīyairapi yodhamukhyaiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And all these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with the hosts of kings, Bhīṣma, Droṇa and that son of a charioteer (sūtaputra), along with the chief warriors of our own side too —
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 11.26–27 form one sentence. sūtaputra is Karṇa, named in 11.34. The vision includes warriors of Arjuna's own side.

original.text:
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti
daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni|
kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu
saṃdṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — hastening, enter your fearful mouths, terrible with tusks; some are seen caught between the teeth, their heads crushed.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ
samudramevābhimukhāḥ dravanti|
tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā
viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: As the many currents of rivers flow toward the ocean alone, so these heroes of the world of men enter your flaming mouths.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṅgā
viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ|
tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokā
stavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: As moths with gathering speed enter a blazing fire to perish, so too the worlds, with gathering speed, enter your mouths to perish.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Two similes in succession: rivers entering the ocean (11.28) and moths entering a flame 'for their destruction' (nāśāya, 11.29).

original.text:
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantā
llokānsamagrānvadanairjvaladbhiḥ|
tejobhirāpūrya jagatsamagraṃ
bhāsastavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick (your lips); your fierce rays, filling the whole world with splendour (tejas), scorch it, Viṣṇu.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ākhyāhi me ko bhavānugrarūpo
namo'stu te devavara prasīda|
vijñātumicchāmi bhavantamādyaṃ
na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Tell me who you are, of fierce form. Homage to you, best of gods; be gracious (prasīda). I wish to know you, the primal one (ādya), for I do not understand your activity (pravṛtti).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: pravṛtti: what you are engaged in, your undertaking; the Lord answers in 11.32 with the same root ('engaged', pravṛtta).

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho
lokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ|
ṛte'pi tvāṃ na bhaviṣyanti sarve
ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time (kāla), grown mighty, the maker of the destruction of the worlds, engaged here in drawing in (samāhartum) the worlds. Even without you, all the warriors drawn up in the opposing ranks will cease to be.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ṛte 'pi tvām: 'even without you', i.e., apart from any action of yours. lokān samāhartum: 'to gather in / withdraw the worlds'. The answer to 'who are you?' (11.31) is given in one word, kāla.

original.text:
tasmāttvamuttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva
jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham|
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvameva
nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Therefore rise up and win glory; conquering your enemies, enjoy a prosperous kingdom. By me alone have these already been struck down; be merely the instrument (nimitta-mātra), left-handed archer (savyasācin).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: tasmāt ('therefore') draws the command from 11.32. nimitta: here the occasion or instrument through which the already-decided outcome comes about. savyasācin: one who draws the bow with the left hand as well.

original.text:
droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca
karṇaṃ tathā'nyānapi yodhavīrān|
mayā hatāṃstvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā
yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Droṇa and Bhīṣma, Jayadratha and Karṇa, and the other warrior heroes as well — already slain by me — do you slay; do not be distressed (mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ); fight: you will conquer your rivals in battle.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
etacchrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya
kṛtāñjalirvepamānaḥ kirīṭī|
namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ
sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Sañjaya said: Having heard these words of Keśava, the crowned one (Kirīṭin), with joined palms, trembling, made obeisance, and, bowing down, spoke again to Kṛṣṇa, stammering, overcome with fear.
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sagadgadam: with a faltering, choked voice; bhītabhītaḥ: 'afraid, afraid' — greatly afraid.

original.text:
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā
jagat prahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca|
rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti
sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṅghāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: Rightly (sthāne), Hṛṣīkeśa, does the world rejoice and delight in your glorification (prakīrti); the rākṣasas, afraid, flee in all directions, and all the hosts of the perfected (siddha) bow down.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sthāne: 'it is fitting that ...'. tava prakīrtyā: by your glorification, i.e., by the praise of you.

original.text:
kasmācca te na nameranmahātman
garīyase brahmaṇo'pyādikartre|
ananta deveśa jagannivāsa
tvamakṣaraṃ sadasattatparaṃ yat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And why should they not bow to you, great being, who are greater even than Brahmā and the first maker (or: greater, the first maker even of Brahmā)? Endless one, lord of gods, abode of the world, you are the imperishable (akṣara), being and non-being (sad asat), that which is beyond (tat paraṃ yat).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: garīyase brahmaṇo 'py ādikartre: 'greater even than Brahmā, the first creator', or 'greater (than all), the first creator even of Brahmā' (brahmaṇaḥ may also be the neuter brahman). tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat tatparaṃ yat: either 'you are the imperishable, being and non-being, and what is beyond both', or 'you are the imperishable that is beyond being and non-being'; commentators divide.

original.text:
tvamādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇa
stvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam|
vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma
tvayā tataṃ viśvamanantarūpa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You are the first god (ādideva), the ancient Person (puruṣa purāṇa); you are the supreme resting-place (nidhāna) of this universe; you are the knower (vettṛ) and what is to be known (vedya), and the supreme abode (dhāman); by you this universe is pervaded (tata), O one of endless form.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ
prajāpatistvaṃ prapitāmahaśca|
namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ
punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon (Śaśāṅka), Prajāpati and the great-grandsire (prapitāmaha). Homage, homage to you a thousand times; and again and yet again, homage, homage to you.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prapitāmaha: 'great-grandfather' — commentators: the father even of the grandsire (Brahmā).

original.text:
namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste
namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva|
anantavīryāmitavikramastvaṃ
sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Homage to you in front and from behind; homage to you on every side, O All (sarva). Of endless strength and immeasurable valour, you encompass (samāpnoṣi) all; therefore you are all (sarva).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse gives its own reason: the Lord is 'all' because he pervades / reaches through all (sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ).

original.text:
sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yaduktaṃ
he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti|
ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedaṃ
mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whatever I said rashly, thinking of you as a friend — 'O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O friend' — not knowing this greatness (mahiman) of yours, whether through heedlessness (pramāda) or through affection (praṇaya),
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 11.41–42 form one sentence ending in the request for forgiveness.

original.text:
yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si
vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu|
eko'thavāpyacyuta tatsamakṣaṃ
tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: and whatever disrespect was shown you in jest, at play, lying down, sitting or eating, alone or in the presence of others, Acyuta — for that I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
pitāsi lokasya carācarasya
tvamasya pūjyaśca gururgarīyān|
na tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo
lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāva
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You are the father of this world, moving and unmoving; you are its object of worship (pūjya) and its weightiest teacher (guru garīyān). There is none equal to you — how then another greater? — in the three worlds, O one of unequalled power.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ
prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍyam|
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Therefore, bowing and prostrating my body, I seek your grace (prasādaye), you the lord who is to be praised. As a father with a son, as a friend with a friend, as a dear one with a beloved, you should bear with me, O god.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: priyaḥ priyāyārhasi: 'as a dear one (bears with) a dear one'; the sandhi is irregular, and the second word is read either as priyāyāḥ ('with the beloved woman') or priyāya ('with a dear one'). The verse names three relations — father–son, friend–friend, lover–beloved — as the measure of the forbearance asked.

original.text:
adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito'smi dṛṣṭvā
bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me|
tadeva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Having seen what was never seen before, I am thrilled (hṛṣita), and my mind (manas) is shaken with fear. Show me, O god, that very form (of yours); be gracious, lord of gods, abode of the world.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Delight and fear are reported together. tad eva rūpam: 'that very form' — the form Arjuna knew before, described in 11.46.

original.text:
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahasta
micchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭumahaṃ tathaiva|
tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena
sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I wish to see you just so — crowned, bearing a mace, discus in hand. Take on that very four-armed form (rūpeṇa caturbhujena), thousand-armed one, whose form is the universe (viśvamūrti).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse asks for 'that very four-armed form'; it does not say when Arjuna saw it. Commentators differ whether it is Kṛṣṇa's familiar form (called 'his own form' and 'this human form' in 11.50–51) or a four-armed form distinct from it. The crown, mace and discus were also seen within the universal form (11.17).

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ
rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt|
tejomayaṃ viśvamanantamādyaṃ
yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Being gracious to you (prasanna), Arjuna, I have shown you by my own yoga (ātma-yoga) this supreme form — made of splendour, universal, endless, primal — which no one other than you has seen before.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmayogāt is reflexive to the speaker: 'by my own yoga (power)'. The showing is grounded in the Lord's being pleased (prasanna).

original.text:
na vedayajñādhyayanairna dānai
rna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ|
evaṃrūpaḥ śakya ahaṃ nṛloke
draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Not by the Vedas, sacrifices or study, not by gifts, not by rites (kriyā), nor by fierce austerities (tapas) can I, in such a form, be seen in the world of men by anyone but you, hero of the Kurus.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: vedayajñādhyayanaiḥ may be divided 'by the Vedas, sacrifices and study' or 'by study of the Vedas and of sacrifices'. The means listed are excluded as means to this particular sight.

original.text:
mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo
dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoramīdṛṅmamedam|
vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvaṃ
tadeva me rūpamidaṃ prapaśya
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Do not be distressed (vyathā), do not be bewildered (vimūḍha-bhāva), at seeing this terrible form of mine; with fear gone and a glad mind (prīta-manas), behold again that very form of mine.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ityarjunaṃ vāsudevastathoktvā
svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ|
āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenaṃ
bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Vāsudeva showed again his own form (svakaṃ rūpam); and the great being (mahātman), becoming again gentle in form (saumya-vapus), comforted the frightened one.
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tavasaumyaṃ janārdana|
idānīmasmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: Seeing this gentle human form (mānuṣaṃ rūpam) of yours, Janārdana, I am now composed, with my awareness restored (sacetāḥ), and have come back to my own nature (prakṛti).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sacetāḥ: 'with (my) cetas', i.e., with awareness restored. prakṛtiṃ gataḥ: 'returned to (my) normal condition' — prakṛti here is Arjuna's natural state, not the Sāṃkhya principle.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
sudurdarśamidaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama|
devā apyasya rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods are ever longing for a sight (darśana) of this form.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

bhaktyā tvananyayā śakyamahamevaṃvidho'rjuna|
jñātuṃ dṛṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca paraṃtapa

paraphrase: Chapter 11 is the vision of the Lord's sovereign, universal form. Movements: (1) 11.1–4 — Arjuna says his delusion is gone through the secret teaching concerning the self, accepts what the Lord has said of himself, and asks, if he is able, to see his sovereign form. (2) 11.5–8 — the Lord bids him behold his manifold divine forms and the whole world standing as one in his body, and, since his own eye cannot see it, gives him a divine eye. (3) 11.9–14 — Sañjaya tells Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the form: many mouths and eyes, divine ornaments and weapons, a light as of a thousand suns, the whole world divided many ways yet standing as one in the god's body; Arjuna, amazed, his hair on end, bows and speaks. (4) 11.15–31 — Arjuna describes what he sees: gods, Brahmā, seers and all beings within the form, without beginning, middle or end; he names it the imperishable, the resting-place of the universe, the guardian of eternal dharma; then the fierce form that makes the worlds and himself tremble, into whose mouths the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa and warriors of both sides rush like rivers into the sea and moths into a flame; he asks who this fierce one is. (5) 11.32–34 — the Lord answers: 'I am Time, grown mighty, destroyer of worlds'; the warriors will perish even without Arjuna; they are already slain by him; Arjuna is to be merely the instrument, and fight. (6) 11.35–46 — trembling, Arjuna praises him as greater than all, the imperishable, being and non-being and what is beyond, the first god, pervading all and therefore all; he asks forgiveness for past familiarity and asks to see again the crowned, four-armed form. (7) 11.47–51 — the Lord says he showed this form by his own yoga, out of grace, and that it cannot be seen by Vedas, sacrifice, study, gifts, rites or austerity; he tells Arjuna not to fear, resumes his gentle form, and Arjuna is restored. (8) 11.52–55 — the form is hard to see even for gods; only by undivided devotion can the Lord be known, seen and entered in truth; whoever does his work, holds him supreme, is devoted, unattached and without enmity toward any being comes to him.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: arjuna uvācaevaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate|yecāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ

paraphrase: Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever yoked in this way (evaṃ satata-yuktāḥ), worship (paryupāsate) you, and those who (worship) the imperishable (akṣara), the unmanifest (avyakta) — of these, which know yoga best (yoga-vittama)?

original.text: śrī bhagavānuvācamayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate|śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ

original.text: śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate|dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram

paraphrase: For knowledge (jñāna) is better than practice (abhyāsa); meditation (dhyāna) is superior to knowledge; the relinquishing of the fruit of actions (karma-phala-tyāga) (is superior) to meditation; from relinquishment, peace (śānti) follows immediately.

paraphrase: Chapter 12 answers which worshippers know yoga best and lays out the practice of devotion. Movements: (1) 12.1 — Arjuna asks: of those devotees who, ever yoked, worship the Lord, and those who worship the imperishable, the unmanifest, which know yoga best? (2) 12.2–7 — the Lord answers that those who fix their mind on him and worship him with supreme faith are the most yoked; those who worship the indefinable, unmanifest, unthinkable imperishable, restraining the senses, even in understanding everywhere, delighting in the welfare of all beings, also reach him, but their hardship is greater, for the unmanifest goal is hard for the embodied; those who lay down all actions in him and meditate on him with undivided yoga he soon lifts from the ocean of death and saṃsāra. (3) 12.8–12 — graded instruction: fix mind and understanding on him; if the thought cannot be held steady, seek him by the yoga of practice; if incapable of practice, be intent on work for him; if unable even that, give up the fruit of all actions; then a ranking — knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge, relinquishing the fruit above meditation, with peace following on relinquishment. (4) 12.13–19 — the marks of the devotee dear to him: without hatred, friendly and compassionate, free of 'mine' and 'I', the same in pleasure and pain, content, self-restrained, neither disturbing nor disturbed by the world, free of elation, intolerance, fear and agitation, without expectation, relinquishing undertakings and both good and evil, the same toward friend and foe, honour and dishonour, praise and blame, silent, homeless, steady in judgement, full of devotion; each group ends with the refrain 'he is dear to me'. (5) 12.20 — those who with faith attend to this nectar of dharma, holding him supreme, are exceedingly dear to him.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
